name: Longest Common Subsequence (LCS)
description: Finds the longest subsequence present in both strings. Uses a 2D DP table where dp[i][j] = LCS length of first i chars of s1 and first j chars of s2.
aim: Find the length of the longest sequence of characters that appears in both strings in the same relative order, but not necessarily contiguous.
howItWorks: Build dp[m+1][n+1] table where m=len(s1), n=len(s2)
Else: dp[i][j] = max(dp[i-1][j], dp[i][j-1]) (skip one char)
Trace back from dp[m][n] to reconstruct the actual LCS

complexity.spaceDescription: 2D table of size (m+1)×(n+1); can optimize to O(min(m,n)) with rolling array

realWorld: Version control diff (git diff) — find common lines
DNA sequence alignment — find common genetic subsequences
whenToUse: Longest common subsequence of two sequences
Foundation for edit distance and other sequence problems
alternatives: Longest Common Substring — requires contiguous match
